findings.evidence: grep -rn 'pipefail|SIGPIPE' docs/internal/standards/*.md returns nothing. docs/internal/standards/portability.md (114 lines, current state) has no shell-scripting section at all -- its 20 rules cover targets/runtime/build/test/cross-arch portability but not this. The idiom is documented only in scattered code comments (scripts/lib.sh:14, scripts/check-layering.sh:79-82, scripts/check-core-contract.sh:70-72, scripts/check-unsafe.sh:102-104, scripts/build-index.sh:45, scripts/check-milestone-review.sh:229/255/277, scripts/milestone-review.sh:89, scripts/check-reviewed.sh:70/80/207, scripts/check-commit-msg.sh:49-52) and in backlog prose, which is tribal knowledge, not a standard any future gate-writer is pointed at before making the ninth-plus mistake.
findings.summary: The set -o pipefail SIGPIPE-under-early-exit defect that recurred nine times across six scripts this milestone (per docs/internal/product/backlog.md's M-1.37 retrospective, ~line 1090, and docs/internal/product/milestones/M-1.md's own 'Notes for the boundary review') was never written into a standard, despite the retrospective explicitly saying 'it belongs in the shell rules portability.md will grow.'

findings.evidence: Chronological order via `git log --oneline --reverse a7574d4..b8bd28e`: fadd095 (M-1.33 follow-up) introduces the try/except-Exception-then-sys.exit(3) wrapper in scripts/build-index.sh; c2704cd (M-1.8, check-layering.sh) and 904724c (M-1.10, check-core-contract.sh) both land after it; b8bd28e (M-1.11, check-unsafe.sh, lines 529-537) explicitly copies the wrapper and cites build-index.sh's precedent in its own comment ('the same fix build-index.sh already applies to itself for the identical reason'). scripts/check-layering.sh and scripts/check-core-contract.sh have no `try:`/`except Exception`/`exit(3)` anywhere (confirmed by grep) -- their crash-safety currently depends entirely on the undocumented fact that no `print()` executes before their risky `.read_text()` / `git show` calls, so a future diagnostic print added before those calls would silently reintroduce exactly the false-pass-on-crash class this milestone's review rounds spent many cycles closing elsewhere.
findings.summary: check-layering.sh and check-core-contract.sh pass safely on an uncaught Python crash only by accident of statement ordering, not by the defended crash-safety wrapper (try/except with a distinct exit code) that build-index.sh established and check-unsafe.sh explicitly reused -- both were written after that idiom existed and neither adopted it.

findings.evidence: scripts/check-reviewed.sh:191 and scripts/check-milestone-review.sh:238 both emit `warn "$BASELINE has unstaged edits, which are ignored..."`; scripts/check-unsafe.sh reads baselines/unsafe.txt via the identical `git show ":$BASELINE"` pattern (line 97) but has no corresponding warn call anywhere in the file (grep for 'unstaged' in check-unsafe.sh returns nothing), even though its own header comment says baselines/unsafe.txt uses 'the same escape-with-a-reason shape baselines/review.txt already uses.'
findings.summary: check-unsafe.sh reads baselines/unsafe.txt from the index (matching baselines/review.txt's convention) but, unlike check-reviewed.sh and check-milestone-review.sh, never warns when the file has unstaged edits, so the 'honest path punished' UX fix M-1.9's retrospective called its sharpest finding was not carried to the baseline file modeled explicitly on the one that motivated it.
